H1b.theory: A Si-rich shell reduces local alloy disorder but adds interface/gradient scattering; net effect depends on shell thickness, with thin shells possibly helping and thicker ones hurting.
H1b.falsifier: Atomistic simulations sweeping shell thickness always show a monotonic decrease in kappa with thickness, which would falsify the disorder-relief vs added-scattering crossover.
H1b.reach: Would change how much of the SiC particle's kappa reduction is attributed to interface scattering versus the surrounding composition.

H5.theory: Tersoff-1989 gives bulk Si kappa higher than DFT-based BTE, by about 2x at 300 K (Tersoff-based transport 305 vs DFT 147 W/mK). The gap is expected to grow at 1100 K because four-phonon scattering lowers the DFT reference faster with temperature.
H5.falsifier: Size-converged homogeneous NEMD with Tersoff-1989 on bulk Si at 300 K and 1100 K that falls within ±30% of the almaBTE values at both temperatures.
H5.reach: If it holds, Tersoff-based MD kappa values for Si-rich systems are biased high relative to the first-principles reference, which affects cross-source comparisons across the campaign.
H5.basis: H5 @1100 K: If the almaBTE reference includes strong high-T resistive physics (especially 4ph), then the comparison category is most likely “Tersoff higher by more than 30%”, unless NEMD length/gradient artifacts reduce κ_Tersoff.

H6.theory: The theories say as-grown substitutional C is metastable and that SiC formation needs a thermal-budget or defect-injection step. They give no formation energies and no numeric Si-vs-Ge neighbour preference for C, so the sign and size of the SiC energy gain are not addressed.
H6.falsifier: A MACE-MP-0 energy comparison of substitutional C versus C in a SiC precipitate in Si0.8Ge0.2.
H6.reach: Determines whether the Si-rich shell and SiC precipitate picture used in the thermal-conductivity runs is energetically justified.

H7.theory: Alloy disorder dominates at x≈0.5, so coherent strain only modestly changes kappa and does so anisotropically. In-plane kappa is unchanged to mildly increased, while cross-plane kappa decreases.
H7.falsifier: Coherent versus relaxed Si0.5Ge0.5 simulations in which cross-plane kappa changes by less than 5% or increases, or changes by more than 25% without dislocations.
H7.reach: If it holds, strain engineering of SiGe films gives only small, anisotropic kappa changes, so films can be compared with relaxed bulk values to within about 10%.
H7.basis: For coherently compressed Si0.5Ge0.5 on Si(001) at 300 K, κ⊥ (cross-plane) will fall slightly relative to relaxed bulk (category: decrease), with a likely magnitude of ~5–12% decrease, while κ∥ increases modestly (few to ~10%) due to in-plane stiffening.
